Product Launch Checklist

A product launch lives or dies on preparation — the loudest launch day can't rescue a product no one was primed for. This checklist runs in order across three phases: the weeks of pre-launch groundwork, the launch itself, and the follow-up that turns a spike into momentum. Adapt the timeline to your product, but keep the sequence. See more business and launch checklists.

Product Launch Checklist · 20 items

  1. 1
    Nail your positioning: who it's for, the problem it solves, and why it's different

    Everything downstream — copy, pricing, targeting — flows from this one paragraph.

  2. 2
    Define the launch goal and the metrics you'll judge it by (signups, revenue, installs)
  3. 3
    Set the launch date and work backward into a dated pre-launch timeline
  4. 4
    Run a private beta and collect feedback, testimonials, and bug reports
  5. 5
    Fix the launch-blocking issues from beta and confirm the release candidate
  6. 6
    Finalize pricing, packaging, and any launch-day offer or trial
  7. 7
    Write the core messaging and prepare the landing or product page
  8. 8
    Prepare launch assets: demo video, screenshots, press kit, and FAQ
  9. 9
    Line up distribution: email list, social posts, communities, and any press or creators

    Warm your audience with teasers before launch day, not on it.

  10. 10
    Set up analytics, event tracking, and dashboards to measure the launch

    Verify events fire in a staging environment before launch day.

  11. 11
    Brief support and sales, and prepare canned answers to the likely questions
  12. 12
    Do a full dry run: test signup, checkout, onboarding, and the support path end to end
  13. 13
    Schedule the launch-day posts, emails, and any submission (directory, marketplace, or press embargo)
  14. 14
    Launch: publish the page, send the announcement, and post across your channels
  15. 15
    Monitor systems, error rates, and payments closely for the first hours
  16. 16
    Engage in real time: reply to comments, questions, and reviews as they come in
  17. 17
    Track results against your launch metrics and note what converted best
  18. 18
    Follow up with leads, trials, and press who engaged but didn't convert
  19. 19
    Gather feedback from new users and triage the first round of fixes
  20. 20
    Run a launch retrospective: what worked, what didn't, and what to repeat next time

Frequently asked questions

What should a product launch checklist include? expand_more

It should span three phases: pre-launch (positioning, beta, pricing, assets, and analytics), launch day (publishing, announcing, and monitoring), and post-launch (following up with leads, gathering feedback, and running a retrospective). Preparation is the bulk of it — launch day is mostly executing what you set up.

How far in advance should I plan a product launch? expand_more

For most products, start four to eight weeks out. That leaves time for a beta, fixing what it surfaces, preparing assets, and warming your audience. Bigger launches with press or a physical product need longer; a small feature can go in a week or two.

What metrics matter for a product launch? expand_more

Pick your metrics before you launch so you know what success looks like. Common ones are signups or installs, activation (people who actually use it), revenue or trial starts, and traffic-to-signup conversion. Tracking which channels drove the best conversions tells you where to invest next time.
